facts.text: Mexico, Maine began as Holmanstown Plantation, granted in 1789 by the Massachusetts General Court to Colonel Jonathan Holman and associates.
The remaining portion of Holmanstown, first settled by Isaac Gleason, became the town of Mexico on February 13, 1818.
Mexico earned its name from local admiration for Mexico's 1810–1821 fight for independence from Spain.
Mexico sits atop several hills that overlook the Androscoggin River, giving the town a scenic high‑ground view.
In the 19th century, the Swift River’s mouth at Mexico’s southwest corner became a historic business hub powered by water.
Ridlon, president of the Rumford Falls Brick Company, founded Ridlonville, a settlement in Mexico’s eastern part, in the early 1800s.
